reasoning: The evidence shows Artemis II is a high-risk mission with several concerning factors: heat shield damage observed after Artemis I requiring trajectory modifications, eight failed tests and recurring leaks reported in late February 2026, untested life support systems with crew, and extreme reentry conditions (40,000 km/h, 2,760°C). However, NASA has implemented extensive safety measures including conservative weather criteria, free-return trajectory, Launch Abort System, and thorough crew training. Historical crewed spaceflight has had ~1-2% fatality rate per mission. The technical issues are concerning but NASA appears to be addressing them systematically. Given the combination of novel mission profile, known technical issues, but also extensive safety preparations, I estimate a low but non-negligible probability.
